```{r}

#| include: false

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)
library(forcats)
library(sf)
library(raster)
library(ipdw)
library(patchwork)
library(here)

# Raw water-quality data
chla_raw <- readRDS(here("2-data", "raw", "chla_raw.rds"))
do_raw <- readRDS(here("2-data", "raw", "do.rds"))
sal_raw <- readRDS(here("2-data", "raw", "salinity_raw.rds"))
turb_raw <- readRDS(here("2-data", "raw", "turb_raw.rds"))
water_temp_raw <- readRDS(here("2-data", "raw", "water_temp_raw.rds"))

raw_data <- list(
  "Chlorophyll-a" = chla_raw,
  "Dissolved Oxygen" = do_raw,
  "Salinity" = sal_raw,
  "Turbidity" = turb_raw,
  "Temperature" = water_temp_raw
)

# Processed water-quality data

do_proc <- readRDS(here("2-data", "processed", "proc_do.rds"))
sal_proc <- readRDS(here("2-data", "processed", "proc_sal.rds"))

water_temp_proc <- readRDS(
  here("2-data", "processed", "proc_water_temp.rds")
)

processed_data <- list(

  "Dissolved Oxygen" = do_proc,
  "Salinity" = sal_proc,
  "Turbidity" = turb_proc,
  "Temperature" = water_temp_proc
)

parameter_units <- c(
  "Chlorophyll-a" = "ug/L",
```

## Water-Quality Data Coverage


<!--
Writing outline: Water-Quality Data Coverage

1. Report the raw observation coverage, then the retained data (@tbl-data-summary).
   - All five parameters combined: 25,665 parameter-specific observations from 174 unique station identifiers. There are 11,946 retained observations, 46.5% of the raw total.
   - Chlorophyll-a: 1,847 raw observations/54 stations; 666 retained observations; 27 bin records, 25 finite means.
   - Dissolved oxygen: 6,261/169; 3,010 retained; 68 bins, all finite. Salinity: 6,994/159; 3,400 retained; 67 bins, all finite.
   - Turbidity: 3,402/146; 1,429 retained; 61 bins, 58 finite means. Temperature: 7,161/169; 3,441 retained; 68 bins, all finite.
   - Distinguish 291 parameter-specific bin rows from 286 finite means. They are not 291 distinct spatial sites because different parameters can share bins. The retained-station column should be checked before calling it exclusively stations with usable non-outlier means.
2. Describe spatial representativeness (@fig-monitoring-coverage).
   - Identify clustering in the western part of the study domain and gaps in the eastern bays from the actual panel maps. Explain the observed basis for excluding chlorophyll-a, without describing a parameter that was dropped as a modeled predictor.
   - Keep actual sampling dates and processing rules in Methods. These coverage counts alone do not establish uniform sampling over the 2005 to 2024 observation period.
-->



There were 25,665 raw observations from across all five parameter datasets, representing 174 unique site locations. Chlorophyll-a had 1,845 records from 54 sites. Processing resulted in 27 binned values using 666. Dissolved Oxygen had 6,261 observations from 169 sites. Processing reduced the data to 68 binned values using 3,010 observations. Salinity returned 6,994 observation values from 159 sites. The data was processed into 67 binned values using 3,400 observations.  Turbidity had 3,402 observed values from 146 sites. After processing there were 61 binned values using 1,429 observations. Water temperature had 7,161 raw observations from 169 sites. Data processing returned 68 binned values using 3,441 observations. Overall, data processing returned 291 parameterized data values using 11,946 fo the 25,665 original values, representing 46.5% of the original dataset (@tbl-data-summary).

For all parameters, the data was heavily skewed spatially, with the majority of samples located in Escambia and Pensacola Bays. Chlorophyll-a in particular had much fewer sites and almost no observations located in the eastern half of the study area. Due to such a lack of spatial distribution, chlorophyll-a was subsequently dropped from the analysis (@fig-monitoring-coverage). 

```{r}
#| label: tbl-data-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Summary of raw and processed warm-season water-quality data by environmental parameter."
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

wq_summary <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Parameter,      ~`Raw observations`, ~`Raw stations`, ~`Retained observations`, ~`Retained stations`, ~`Spatial bins`,
  "Chlorophyll-a", 1847,                54,              666,                      48,                   27,
  "Dissolved Oxygen",            6261,                169,             3010,                     145,                  68,
  "Salinity",      6994,                159,             3400,                     135,                  67,
  "Turbidity",     3402,                146,             1429,                     122,                  61,
  "Temperature",   7161,                169,             3441,                     145,                  68
)

knitr::kable(
  wq_summary,
  booktabs = TRUE,
  align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"),
  digits = 0,
  format.args = list(big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-monitoring-coverage
#| fig-cap: "Spatial distribution of monitoring stations represented in each raw water-quality dataset."
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

monitoring_sites <- imap_dfr(
  raw_data,
  \(data, parameter) {
    data %>%
      dplyr::select(Location_Identifier, geometry) %>%
      dplyr::filter(!is.na(Location_Identifier)) %>%
      dplyr::group_by(Location_Identifier) %>%
      dplyr::slice(1) %>%
      dplyr::ungroup() %>%
      dplyr::mutate(parameter = parameter)
  }
) %>%
  st_as_sf() %>%
  st_transform(st_crs(study_area))

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(
    data = study_area,
    fill = "grey95",
    color = "grey45",
    linewidth = 0.25
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    data = monitoring_sites,
    color = "#2166AC",
    size = 0.7,
    alpha = 0.65
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~parameter, ncol = 2) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

## Environmental Predictor Results


<!--
Writing outline: Environmental Predictor Results

1. Summarize the sensitivity comparison before individual parameters.
   - 36 power/range settings per parameter, five random five-fold spatial partitions. Final chosen settings are power 0.25 and range 10 km for all four WQP surfaces (@fig-ipdw-sensitivity; @tbl-ipdw-validation).
   - Distinguish the lowest-MAE setting from the chosen setting. Use the sensitivity figure for the candidate comparisons and the validation table for repeated performance at the selected settings.
   - The summary statistics below describe means and SDs across five spatial partitions. Signed bias is predicted minus observed. Different measurement units prevent ranking predictor quality solely by raw MAE magnitude.
2. Add recruitment as its own predictor result, even though the current panels omit it.
   - Ten input sites span 0 to 14.76 in the original recruitment units, still to be supplied. Saved validation: MAE 5.510, RMSE 6.481, bias -0.808, 10/10 valid pairs. These values are a separate saved validation summary, not a five-seed sensitivity mean.
   - Recruitment raster: 33,323 finite 100 m cells, range 0 to 14.76, mean 7.354, SD 3.035. Confirm the fold design and source units before writing the validation sentence. Source: stats_oys_rec.rds and rast_oys_rec.tif.
   - Add recruitment to the shared figure/table or provide a separate labeled output before referring to it as shown there. Do not imply depth was a fitted predictor.
-->



Each parameter (save for chlorophyll-a) was interpolated into predicted surface rasters using an inverse-path distance weighting algorithm. To ensure the highest accuracy was achieved, a sensitivy analysis was conducted on each parameter model using 36 distance-power/range combinations, which were in turn evaluated across five random five-fold spatial partitions. Powers ranged from 0.25 to 3.00, and  maximum range values evaluated were 5, 10, 15, and 20 km (@fig-ipdw-sensitivity). 

While the results of every sensitivity analysis will be reported here, it should be noted that after running all parameters it was decided that a distance power of 0.25 and a max range of 10km was to be used. This decision was made as there was little variation in results of the sensitivity analysis and a smoother prediction surface was preferred to better represent the smoother gradients found in the real world. 

```{r}
#| label: fig-ipdw-sensitivity
#| fig-cap: "Mean MAE across distance-power and maximum-range combinations evaluated using repeated five-fold spatial cross-validation. Red outlines identify the parameter combinations used for the final interpolation models."
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 8
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

plot_sensitivity <- function(result, stats, parameter) {
  power_levels <- sort(unique(result$summary$dist_power))
  range_levels <- sort(unique(result$summary$max_range))

  plot_data <- result$summary %>%
    mutate(
      dist_power = factor(dist_power, levels = power_levels),
      max_range = factor(max_range, levels = range_levels)
    )

  selected_data <- result$summary %>%
    filter(
      near(dist_power, stats$dist_power[[1]]),
      max_range == stats$max_range[[1]]
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      dist_power = factor(dist_power, levels = power_levels),
      max_range = factor(max_range, levels = range_levels)
    )

  ggplot(
    plot_data,
    aes(
      x = dist_power,
      y = max_range,
      fill = mean_MAE
    )
  ) +
    geom_tile() +
    geom_tile(
      data = selected_data,
      fill = NA,
      color = "red",
      linewidth = 1.2
    ) +
    geom_text(
      aes(
        label = sprintf("%.2f", mean_MAE),
        color = mean_MAE > median(mean_MAE, na.rm = TRUE)
      ),
      size = 3
    ) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(
      direction = -1,
      name = "Mean MAE"
    ) +
    scale_color_manual(
      values = c("FALSE" = "black", "TRUE" = "white"),
      guide = "none"
    ) +
    labs(
      title = parameter,
      x = "Distance power",
      y = "Maximum range (m)"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
    )
}

sensitivity_plots <- imap(
  sensitivity_results,
  \(result, parameter) {
    plot_sensitivity(
      result = result,
      stats = model_stats[[parameter]],
      parameter = parameter
    )
  }
)

wrap_plots(sensitivity_plots, ncol = 2) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "IPDW Parameter Sensitivity Analysis",
    subtitle = "Repeated five-fold spatial cross-validation"
  )
```

### Dissolved Oxygen

Dissolved oxygen sensitivity had a mean MAE ranging from 0.426 to 0.507 mg/L. The lowest mean MAE with 100% prediction was 0.425mg/L using a distance power of 0.75 and max range of 10km (@tbl-ipdw-validation). The predicted rater surface values ranged from 5.28mg/L to 7.99mg/L (n = 33,792; µ = 6.52; σ = 0.26; @tbl-raster-summary). The final prediction model achieved 100% coverage with a MAE of 0.431 mg/L (σ = 0.006) with RMSE = 0.552 mg/L (σ = 0.004). The model tended to over predict by +0.013 mg/L. Spatially, dissolved oxygen generally decreased in the western portions of the study area. With the lowest values appearing in East Bay and northern Blackwater Bay (@fig-environmental-rasters).   


### Salinity

The salinity sensitivity analysis had a mean MAE ranging from 2.397 ppt to 3.125 ppt. The lowest reported MAE with 100% model coverage was 2.49 ppt using distance power 0.50 and max range of 10km. The absolute lowest mean MAE was 2.397 ppt was achieved using distance power of 3.00 and a max range of 5km , but model coverage fell to 96.1%. The difference in mean MAE between the lowest achieved DP-MR combination and the actual DP-MR combination used was 0.000119 ppt (@tbl-ipdw-validation). Spatial cross-validation of the final model fit had a MAE of 2.49 ppt (σ = 0.036) and RMSE 3.444 ppt (σ = 0.024). The model slightly over predicted salinity values (+0.140 ppt) and achieved 100% coverage. The predicted values ranged from 2.31 to 26.73 ppt (n = 33,792; µ = 16.36 ppt; σ = 3.14; @tbl-raster-summary). Spatially, salinity generally decreased from west to east with the lowest values being in the northern Blackwater Bay and the highest values located in the southwestern region of Pensacola Bay (@fig-environmental-rasters). 

### Turbidity

1. Report sensitivity and selected validation.

   - Selected 0.25/10 km: MAE 0.745 (SD 0.018), RMSE 0.937 (SD 0.026), bias -0.010 NTU, coverage 95.1% (@tbl-ipdw-validation).
   - Coverage is 58 valid observed/predicted pairs divided by 61 rows. The three excluded pairs have nonfinite observed bin means after outlier screening, so do not attribute the entire 4.9% shortfall to interpolation failure.
2. Describe the surface (@fig-environmental-rasters).
   - 33,790 finite cells; range 0.03 to 5.23 NTU; mean 2.229, SD 0.470. Describe the broad north/south contrast visible in the map; support any precise river-mouth claim with the panel itself.

The sensitivity analysis for turbidity reported a mean MAE range from 0.696 to 0.847 NTU. The lowest mean MAE was 0.696 NTU (DP = 1.00, MR = 15km) with 95.1% model coverage (@tbl-ipdw-validation). The final model fit produced a MAE = 0.745 NTU (σ = 0.018) with RMSE = 0.937 NTU (σ = 0.026). Overall the model slightly under predicted by -0.010 NTU and achieved 95.1% coverage. The final predicted surface values ranged from 0.03 NTU to 5.23 NTU (n = 33,790; µ = 2.23 NTU; σ = 0.47; @tbl-raster-summary). Spatially, turbidity generally decreased from north to south, with the highest values occuring near the mouth of Escambia River and the lowest values occuring in the southwestern portion of Pensacola Bay (@fig-environmental-rasters).

Mean MAE for the water temperature sensitivity analysis ranged from 0.978 to 1.135 degrees C. The lowest mean MAE was 0.978 degrees C with 100% model coverage (DP = 0.75, MR = 10km; @tbl-ipdw-validation). The final model had a MAE of 0.988 degrees C (σ = 0.015) and RMSE was 1.163 degrees C (σ = 0.014). The model generally under predicted water temperature by -0.063 degrees C with 100% model coverage. The resulting prediction surface ranged from 25.93 to 30.43 degrees C (n = 33,792; µ = 27.66°C; σ = 0.41°C; @tbl-raster-summary). Water temperature was generally lower in the eastern portions of the study area, with the coolest values trending toward Blackwater Bay (@fig-environmental-rasters).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-ipdw-validation
#| tbl-cap: "Selected IPDW parameters and repeated spatial cross-validation performance. Values in parentheses are standard deviations across random spatial partitions."
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

validation_summary <- imap_dfr(
  model_stats,
  \(stats, parameter) {
    selected_power <- stats$dist_power[[1]]
    selected_range <- stats$max_range[[1]]

    repeated_results <- sensitivity_results[[parameter]]$summary %>%
      filter(
        near(dist_power, selected_power),
        max_range == selected_range
      ) %>%
      slice(1)

    tibble(
      Parameter = parameter,
      Units = parameter_units[[parameter]],
      `Distance power` = selected_power,
      `Maximum range (km)` = selected_range / 1000,
      `Mean MAE (SD)` = sprintf(
        "%.3f (%.3f)",
        repeated_results$mean_MAE,
        repeated_results$sd_MAE
      ),
      `Mean RMSE (SD)` = sprintf(
        "%.3f (%.3f)",
        repeated_results$mean_RMSE,
        repeated_results$sd_RMSE
      ),
      `Mean bias` = sprintf(
        "%.3f",
        repeated_results$mean_Bias
      ),
      `Mean coverage` = scales::percent(
        repeated_results$mean_coverage,
        accuracy = 0.1
      )
    )
  }
)

kable(
  validation_summary,
  booktabs = TRUE,
  align = c("l", "l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r")
)
```

## MaxEnt Model Tuning and Selection


<!--
Writing outline: MaxEnt Model Tuning and Selection

1. Identify the selected configuration and the selection basis.
   - 24 candidates and 96 partition evaluations. Selected LQH with regularization multiplier 0.5; 14 nonzero coefficients. Lowest mean 10th-percentile omission, with highest mean CBI breaking the tie [@Kass2021].
   - Selected AICc 691.295, delta AICc 13.590, compared with the minimum-AICc LQ/0.5 model at AICc 677.705. That alternative has validation AUC 0.520 and omission 22.22%. The selected model is not the minimum-AICc candidate.
   - Source tables: maxent_selected_settings.csv, maxent_tuning_results.csv, and maxent_tuning_partition_metrics.csv. @tbl-maxent-selection is an existing but disabled placeholder requiring these current inputs and columns.
2. Report internal validation with variability.
   - Mean validation AUC 0.703 (SD 0.136); mean 10th-percentile omission 11.46% (SD 9.10 percentage points); mean CBI 0.093 (SD 0.525). Fold CBI values are 0.161, -0.570, 0.069, and 0.712. Training AUC 0.862, stated separately.
   - Fold 1: AUC 0.843, omission 11.1%; fold 2: 0.582, 0%; fold 3: 0.590, 22.2%; fold 4: 0.796, 12.5%. The unweighted fold means give each partition equal weight.
   - Identify these as the same folds used during tuning, without calling them independent final validation or evidence of uniformly strong performance [@Roberts2017; @Kass2021]. Definitions are available in @tbl-eval-metrics, with CBI still needing to be added.
-->





```{r}
#| label: tbl-maxent-selection
#| tbl-cap: "Performance of the leading candidate MaxEnt configurations."
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| eval: false

maxent_tuning <- readRDS(
  here("2-data", "models", "maxent_tuning_results.rds")
)

maxent_tuning_table <- maxent_tuning %>%
  arrange(desc(selected), delta_aicc) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10) %>%
  transmute(
    `Feature class` = feature_class,
    `Regularization multiplier` = regularization_multiplier,
    `Mean AUC` = sprintf("%.3f", mean_auc),
    `Mean omission rate` = sprintf("%.3f", mean_omission_rate),
    `Mean Boyce index` = sprintf("%.3f", mean_boyce),
    `Delta AICc` = sprintf("%.2f", delta_aicc),
    Selected = if_else(selected, "Yes", "No")
  )

kable(
  maxent_tuning_table,
  booktabs = TRUE,
  align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "c")
)
```

## Environmental-Variable Influence


<!--
Writing outline: Environmental-Variable Influence

1. Describe current fitted responses once the relevant output is available.
   - Evaluate dissolved oxygen, salinity, turbidity, temperature, and recruitment curves, plus sediment-category contrasts. Report only ranges/peaks supported by the actual curves, specifying how the other predictors were held constant [@Elith2011; @Merow2013].
   - The model notebook generates numeric-predictor response plots using ENMeval::evalplot.respCurve. The saved maxnet object has 14 nonzero coefficients, but their magnitudes span different feature transformations and are not directly comparable importance percentages.
2. Keep missing evidence explicit.
   - No current saved contribution/permutation importance table or response-curve RDS exists for the report. Older dismo percentages, including salinity 43.77% and oxygen 38.06%, belong to an earlier model and must not be reused.
   - @fig-variable-importance and @fig-response-curves are disabled placeholders. Do not state numerical importance rankings, ecological optima, or response directions until current outputs are supplied. Associations also do not establish ecological causation [@Dormann2013; @Elith2011].

```{r}
#| label: fig-variable-importance
#| fig-cap: "Relative contribution and permutation importance of environmental predictors in the selected MaxEnt model."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 6
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| eval: false

variable_importance <- readRDS(
  here("2-data", "models", "maxent_variable_importance.rds")
)

importance_long <- variable_importance %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(contribution, permutation_importance),
    names_to = "metric",
    values_to = "importance"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    metric = recode(
      metric,
      contribution = "Contribution",
      permutation_importance = "Permutation importance"
    ),
    variable = fct_reorder(variable, importance, .fun = max)
  )

ggplot(
  importance_long,
  aes(
    x = importance,
    y = variable,
    fill = metric
  )
) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#2166AC", "#B2182B")) +
  labs(
    x = "Importance (%)",
    y = NULL,
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-response-curves
#| fig-cap: "Response curves for environmental predictors included in the selected MaxEnt model."

response_curves <- readRDS(
  here("2-data", "models", "maxent_response_curves.rds")
)

ggplot(

  aes(
    x = value,
    y = suitability
  )
) +
  geom_line(color = "#2166AC", linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~variable, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(
    x = "Environmental value",
    y = "Predicted suitability"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Comparison with the Existing HSI


<!--
Writing outline: Comparison with the Existing HSI

1. State the shared comparison area and methods before reporting agreement.
   - Reproducing the existing comparison steps with the saved rasters gives 31,774 paired 100 m cells, 317.74 square km. This is 681 cells/6.81 square km fewer than the complete MaxEnt domain because HSI values are unavailable there.
   - Exact agreement across five equal-width classes: 8,750 cells (27.54%); within one class, including exact matches: 73.38%; continuous Spearman rho: 0.273. HSI class is higher in 17,911 cells (56.37%); MaxEnt class is higher in 5,113 (16.09%). These are descriptive model-comparison results, not validation against field truth [@Johnson2005].
   - Report the five class boundaries and denominator. Equal numeric intervals do not guarantee that two differently constructed model scales have equivalent biological meaning [@Geselbracht2024; @Elith2011].
2. Add the spatial comparison output and describe only supported geography.
   - @tbl-hsi-comparison, @fig-hsi-comparison, and @fig-hsi-scatter exist as labels but remain disabled. The table currently calculates other metrics instead of the exact/within-one class statistics above; update its planned contents to match the chosen comparison.
   - Current comparison code defines difference as HSI class minus MaxEnt class. Identify same-class areas, HSI-higher areas, and MaxEnt-higher areas after the map has been generated and checked. hsi_suitability.png and model_favorability.png are not currently present; no geographic agreement statement can yet be verified from those outputs.
   - Record that these metrics were reproduced from 3-scripts/5-hsi-comparison.qmd against normalized_suitability.tif, maxent_suitability.tif, and complete_mask.tif, rather than copied from a saved comparison CSV.
-->

```{r}
#| label: tbl-hsi-comparison
#| tbl-cap: "Cell-level comparison between MaxEnt and HSI habitat-suitability predictions."
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| eval: false

maxent_suitability <- readRDS(
  here("2-data", "models", "maxent_suitability.rds")
)

hsi_suitability <- readRDS(
  here("2-data", "models", "hsi_suitability.rds")
)

compareRaster(
  maxent_suitability,
  hsi_suitability,
  extent = TRUE,
  rowcol = TRUE,
  crs = TRUE,
  res = TRUE,
  orig = TRUE,
  stopiffalse = TRUE
)

comparison_data <- tibble(
  maxent = getValues(maxent_suitability),
  hsi = getValues(hsi_suitability)
) %>%
  drop_na()

hsi_comparison <- tibble(
  Metric = c(
    "Pearson correlation",
    "Spearman correlation",
    "Mean signed difference",
    "Mean absolute difference",
    "Root mean square difference",
    "Cells within 0.10 suitability units"
  ),
  Value = c(
    sprintf("%.3f", cor(comparison_data$maxent, comparison_data$hsi)),
    sprintf(
      "%.3f",
      cor(
        comparison_data$maxent,
        comparison_data$hsi,
        method = "spearman"
      )
    ),
    sprintf(
      "%.3f",
      mean(comparison_data$maxent - comparison_data$hsi)
    ),
    sprintf(
      "%.3f",
      mean(abs(comparison_data$maxent - comparison_data$hsi))
    ),
    sprintf(
      "%.3f",
      sqrt(mean((comparison_data$maxent - comparison_data$hsi)^2))
    ),
    scales::percent(
      mean(abs(comparison_data$maxent - comparison_data$hsi) <= 0.10),
      accuracy = 0.1
    )
  )
)

kable(
  hsi_comparison,
  booktabs = TRUE,
  align = c("l", "r")
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-hsi-comparison
#| fig-cap: "Spatial comparison of MaxEnt and HSI habitat-suitability predictions. Positive differences indicate greater suitability predicted by MaxEnt."
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 5
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| eval: false

suitability_difference <- maxent_suitability - hsi_suitability

difference_limit <- max(
  abs(range(getValues(suitability_difference), na.rm = TRUE))
)

old_par <- par(
  mfrow = c(1, 3),
  mar = c(2, 2, 3, 5)
)

raster::plot(
  maxent_suitability,
  col = hcl.colors(100, "YlGn"),
  zlim = c(0, 1),
  main = "MaxEnt",
  axes = FALSE,
  box = FALSE
)

raster::plot(
  hsi_suitability,
  col = hcl.colors(100, "YlGn"),
  zlim = c(0, 1),
  main = "HSI",
  axes = FALSE,
  box = FALSE
)

raster::plot(
  suitability_difference,
  col = hcl.colors(100, "Blue-Red 3"),
  zlim = c(-difference_limit, difference_limit),
  main = "MaxEnt minus HSI",
  axes = FALSE,
  box = FALSE
)

par(old_par)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-hsi-scatter
#| fig-cap: "Cell-level relationship between MaxEnt and HSI habitat-suitability predictions. The dashed line represents perfect agreement."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 6
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| eval: false

set.seed(42)

comparison_plot_data <- comparison_data %>%
  slice_sample(n = min(20000, n()))

ggplot(
  comparison_plot_data,
  aes(
    x = hsi,
    y = maxent
  )
) +
  geom_point(
    color = "#2166AC",
    alpha = 0.15,
    size = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_abline(
    slope = 1,
    intercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "grey30"
  ) +
  coord_equal(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(
    x = "HSI suitability",
    y = "MaxEnt suitability"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
